headline: Tariff refunds and CAM gain boost profit, guidance raised
summary_short: Stanley Black & Decker's Q2 FY2026 net sales were $3,961M, up 0.4% y/y and 3.0% q/q, with GAAP EPS of $2.33 (adjusted EPS $1.57) lifted by a $273.7M gain on the CAM divestiture, alongside a $1.7B debt paydown and $250M of share buybacks.
summary_long: Net sales of $3,961M were roughly flat y/y (+0.4%) and up 3.0% q/q, as +3% organic growth and currency tailwinds offset the CAM divestiture and the outdoor licensing transition. Gross margin rose 600bp to 33.0%, aided by ~250bp of net tariff-refund benefit. GAAP EPS of $2.33 and EBIT of $595M include a $273.7M gain on the CAM sale; adjusted EPS was $1.57. The company reduced debt by $1.7B and repurchased $250M of shares in the quarter, ending with $592M of cash and $4,812M of total debt. FY2026 guidance was raised: GAAP EPS to $4.60-$5.45, adjusted EPS to $5.20-$5.80, and free cash flow to $600-$800M.

drivers.explanation: Net sales were flat y/y as +3% volume (led by U.S. retail and C&I channels) and +1% currency tailwind were offset by the CAM divestiture and the gas walk-behind licensing transition; organic revenue grew 3%.
Gross margin rose 600bp to 33.0% on net productivity gains and favorable mix, plus roughly 250bp of benefit from net tariff refunds.
Moves as the arithmetic counterpart of gross-margin expansion: with net sales roughly flat, cost of revenue fell both q/q and y/y as margin rose to 33.0%.
Tools & Outdoor segment margin rose 400bp and Engineered Fastening margin rose 580bp y/y on productivity gains and favorable mix, plus about 150bp/50bp of net tariff-refund benefit respectively.

Lifted primarily by a $273.7M pre-tax gain on the sale of the CAM business completed in April, partially offset by footprint/restructuring charges; this is a one-time item, not organic operating improvement.
Tracks the EBIT swing and includes the same $273.7M CAM divestiture gain, so the q/q and y/y increases substantially overstate underlying operating momentum.
Tracks the EBIT increase driven by the $273.7M CAM sale gain, net of the same footprint/restructuring charges and interest expense.
GAAP net income includes the CAM sale gain; adjusted EPS of $1.57 (vs. GAAP EPS of $2.33) strips this and other non-GAAP items per the release's own reconciliation, giving a cleaner run-rate view.
Follows net income; GAAP EPS of $2.34 includes the same CAM-gain benefit as diluted EPS, versus adjusted EPS of $1.57.
Follows net income growth; diluted GAAP EPS of $2.33 included roughly $0.17 of net tariff-refund benefit plus the CAM sale gain, per the release.
Operating cash flow of $763M plus CAM sale proceeds more than covered the quarter's $1.7B debt paydown and $250M of buybacks, leaving cash higher q/q and y/y.

Company-disclosed $1.7B of quarterly debt reduction is not visible in the long-term debt balance, which is roughly unchanged q/q; the reduction shows up mainly in short-term debt and/or gross debt actions not itemized in these two line items.
Short-term debt fell to $54M from $849.6M a year ago, consistent with the company's broader deleveraging; the release does not itemize which specific notes were retired.
Modest q/q and y/y declines reflect $250M of share buybacks and dividends paid exceeding retained-earnings growth from net income; not separately itemized in the release.
Share count fell as the company repurchased approximately 3.2 million shares for $250 million during the quarter under the Board's April 2026 authorization.

Management (CEO Chris Nelson, CFO Patrick Hallinan) frames Q2 as on track for full-year sales and margin targets, citing tariff-refund tailwinds, the closed CAM divestiture, $1.7B of debt reduction, $250M of buybacks, and raised FY2026 EPS and free-cash-flow guidance.
